newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan forces pound Tamil Tiger rebel bases.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan forces pound Tamil Tiger rebel bases.

text.p: Sri Lankan forces launched simultaneous air, naval and artillery attacks on key Tamil Tiger rebel bases in northeastern jungles early on Thursday, inflicting heavy casualties, military officials said.

"Air force pilots have reported direct hits on targets," an official told Reuters. "Ground troops monitoring rebel radio transmissions say the rebels have suffered heavy casualties and are asking for reinforcements."

Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels were believed to have suffered casualties in the combined offensive and were also calling for reinforcements, according to rebel radio traffic monitored by the army, they said.
The attacks were centered around the LTTE's so-called "14 base" complex in the jungles of the northeastern Mullaitivu district, 280 km (175 miles) from the capital Colombo, the officials said.
"LTTE camps in the area were pounded for three or four hours starting at dawn," an official said.
Bases for the rebels' Sea Tiger naval wing were also attacked, he said.
Several camps in the base complex and others on the coast were destroyed, the officials said. The offensive followed intelligence reports of a rebel build-up in preparation for an attack, they added.
LTTE rebels overran a key Sri Lanka military camp in the area last year, killing more than 1,000 soldiers.
The Tigers are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the number is higher.
